_about: Charging tools. Hold the use button: the charge goes up one step every charge_seconds, up to max_charge[tool level - 1]. Each charge step has an area drawn with the farmer facing down: '@' is the farmer's cell, '#' a cell the tool works on, rows below '@' are ahead. Hammer and axe hit one cell harder instead (hits). Using a tool gives experience (exp_per_swing: work = the swing changed a cell, miss = it hit nothing; a use that never swung gives none). exp_to_level[i] is the total a tool needs to go from level i+1 to i+2; level_up is the message (%d = the new level). Numbers are ours.

master._about: A charging tool at its top level (level 5 adds no charge step) costs stamina_pct percent of a swing's stamina, rounded up, at least 1. The swing's work fatigue is unchanged; overwork comes only from missing stamina, so it drops too. level_up is added to that tool's level-up message. Numbers are ours.

rod._about: The fishing rod doesn't charge: a tap casts it (stamina per cast) at the first water cell up to reach cells ahead. Bites and fish: data/fish.json. 4 a cast (was 2): about a fish a cast, so the stamina left after field work is what limits a day's fishing; at 2 the year playtest fished the river six hours a day and fish out-earned the crops three to one (WORKLOG 2026-11-03).

hoe.level_up: The hoe bites into the soil more easily. Hoe level %d!

can.level_up: You have a feel for the watering can now. Can level %d!

hammer._exp_to_level: Like the sickle's: the mine is all hammer work, so with the axe's numbers the year playtest had it at level 4 after one spring and 5 in fall of year 1, and the smithy's hammer upgrades were never needed (WORKLOG 2026-11-03).
hammer.level_up: Your hammer blows land true. Hammer level %d!

axe.level_up: The axe sits lighter in your hands. Axe level %d!
